introduction_markdown: Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, June 2020, Ordinary Level, Physics, Paper 2 (subject code 0580). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown: On a hot afternoon, it is cooler inside a house with a thatched roof than in the neighbouring house roofed with aluminium. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Thatch is a **poor conductor** of heat (a good thermal insulator) because it traps air, so little of the Sun's heat passes through the roof into the house. Aluminium is a **good conductor** (and absorbs the heat of the Sun), so heat flows quickly through the roof and makes the inside of the house hotter.

questions.enonce_markdown: When two blocks of ice are pressed against each other, they stick together after they are released. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Pressing the blocks together increases the pressure at the contact surface. A higher pressure **lowers the melting point of ice**, so a thin layer of ice melts. When the pressure is released the melting point rises back, the water **refreezes** and joins the two blocks together (this is called regelation).

questions.enonce_markdown: Steam, rather than boiling water, is used for determining the upper fixed point of a thermometer. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown: Impurities in water change its boiling point, but the steam above boiling water is always **pure**. The temperature of the steam is constant ($100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ at standard atmospheric pressure) whatever the impurities in the water, so it gives a reliable fixed point.
